body:
Global crypto markets pulled back sharply on Wednesday as the total market cap fell to $2.67T, down 4.29% over 24 hours on volume of $88.6B. The session had the unmistakable texture of profit-taking after a violent 7-day rally across virtually every major asset, and the Fear and Greed index confirmed that dynamic, dropping from 74 to 65 in a single day. That one-point decline in the greed reading may look modest on paper, but CoinDesk is already flagging that the gauge has hit its highest levels since just before October's $19 billion liquidation event, which should sharpen everyone's risk discipline heading into the back half of the week. BTC dominance sits at 59.2% with ETH dominance at 11.1%, and the relative strength of those figures against a broad altcoin selloff tells you exactly where institutional hands are parking capital when nerves creep in.

Bitcoin printed $78,998 on the session, off 1.86% over 24 hours on volume of $34.43B, though the 1-hour move of just -0.10% suggests the rate of decline has stalled near current levels. The $79,000 handle is now the line traders are watching with real intensity: the asset held it through most of the day, and CoinDesk's headline specifically notes that Bitcoin is holding $79,000 while the rest of the complex slips. On the weekly basis BTC is still up 22.90%, so the pullback is contained relative to the gains booked. CryptoQuant is calling this the initial phase of a new bull market but flags $83,000 as the level that needs to break convincingly before the thesis firms up, and that framing tracks with what the tape is showing right now — constructive structure, not yet confirmed breakout.

ETH held up better than almost anything else in the complex, down just 1.32% over 24 hours to $2,465.06 on $12.86B in volume, making it the best performer among ZIMR tracked majors for the session. Its 7-day gain of 28.80% and UNI's 28.40% weekly move suggest the Ethereum ecosystem caught a genuine bid during the rally rather than just riding beta. The real pain today was in the higher-beta names: ADA collapsed 5.97% to $0.210219, DOT fell 5.77% to $0.856838, SOL dropped 4.37% to $97.03, and XRP gave back 4.27% to $1.44. That XRP number deserves particular attention — CoinDesk reports that the token's 44% 7-day rally has brought leverage back into the market in size, explicitly raising the risk of a sharper pullback, and the session's move looks like that process beginning. SOL's volume of $3.91B on a down day indicates active selling rather than passive drift, and LINK at $11.35 with only $0.39B in volume looks thin and vulnerable if sentiment rolls further.

The macro backdrop is doing real work here, and not all of it is bearish. BlackRock is reported to have cut the minimum swap size for its bitcoin ETF to $1 million, a structural change that widens the pool of eligible participants and explains in part why Cointelegraph notes that bitcoin ETFs have torn through their 2026 outflows in a 7-day hot streak. That is the kind of institutional plumbing improvement that matters for sustained demand, not just a sentiment headline. On the regulatory and infrastructure side, US state banking associations are planning to launch a nationwide blockchain network targeting 2027, a development that adds legitimacy to the space even if the timeline is too long to trade directly. World Liberty Financial launching USD1 natively on the Canton Network adds another data point to the stablecoin infrastructure buildout that has been a quiet but persistent theme this quarter.

The key watch items from here are straightforward. Bitcoin's ability to defend $79,000 on any further selling pressure is the immediate binary — a clean close below that level would likely trigger a cascade into the altcoin complex that is already under stress. The $83,000 level cited by CryptoQuant is the upside catalyst that would confirm the bull market characterization and likely pull ETH through $2,600 in its wake. The XRP leverage situation is a known risk that the market has been explicitly warned about, so any spike in volatility there should be read as a contagion signal rather than isolated noise. The Fear and Greed reading at 65 is elevated but not yet extreme, and a further decline toward 50 would actually be healthy; a spike back toward 80 without a price catalyst would be a red flag. Watch the ETF flow data tomorrow morning — if inflows continue against today's price weakness, that's the cleanest bullish signal in the tape.
